newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher, Mishtanim at record.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher, Mishtanim at record.

text.p: Israeli shares rose on Monday carrying the Mishatanim index above 300 points for the first time, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.39 percent, or 4.14 points, to 302.77 on all-share turnover of 210 million shekels against 151 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.51 percent higher at 309.47.
Analysts said the rise was unconnected to the appointment of Yaacov Neeman as finance minister.

"I don't think today's gains were a result of the Neeman appointment," said Gidi Halpern of Meitav Investments and Securities. "If Sharon had been appointed, the market would have gone down. But Neeman didn't boost it."

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu named Neeman to the finance portfolio on Monday morning. National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon, distrusted by the market, had been the leading candidate for the post.

"Neeman's appointment is only one part of a much bigger picture. The market wanted to rise but the political uncertainty and the shekel's volatility prevented it from rising. Now the shekel is stabilising and it seems that the government surrvived this crisis," said Julien Assous at Sahar Securities.

Share prices have been rising over the past week after the market's nine-month rally was knocked off balance at the end of June by a sharp depreciation of the Israeli shekel. The shekel has since regained some of its losses against the dollar and has stabilised.

Halpern said the market was "good but not strong", pointing to low demand in the morning leader and declining turnovers to the 150 million-170 million shekel level a day this week from 250 million shekels daily two weeks ago.
"There is still an element of uncertainty concerning the level of the market, what will happen with interest rataes and the direction of the dollar," Halpern said.

Assous said investors are nevertheless bullish. "There is a consensus in the market that the positive trend will continue as investors anticipate a second wave of public offerings next month," he said.
A trader at Bank Leumi said the fact that the market broke a technical barrier on Monday on higher volume is a clear indication that the trend is positive.
"Activity is rising and bonds are becoming less attractive, which is bringing more new money into the market," he said.
Koor Industries, the most active share, surged 4.75 percent to 33,159 agorot on volume of 13.1 million shekels.

Last week Stanley Gold, Koor's chairman and president of Shamrock Holdings, said he would propose Koor spin off its biggest publicly traded subsidiaries to shareholders. On Monday Koor said it intended to go ahead with five-year strategic expansion plan.
"I don't think that Koor rose because of expectations for a spin off. The share has been suffering from a negative bias for a long time and now it is recovering," Assous said.

Other active shares included Bank Hapoalim, which gained 1.0 percent to 779 agorot on turnover of 9.4 million shekels, and Bank Leumi, which rose 1.0 percent to 568 agorot on turnover of 7.9 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
